_provenance: Hand-derived from the written ordering rules (cmdbar.py match_commands/fuzzy_matches and the Rust contract), NOT generated by running Rust. Each derivation states the keys so a reviewer can re-check it by hand.

prefix.derivation: All four match case-insensitively. Case-sensitive prefix 'Li' gives rank 1 to Line, LinearDimension, Limit; 'line' is rank 2. Rank-1 group sorted by lowercase name: 'limit' < 'line' < 'lineardimension'.
'line' and 'Line' equal the query case-insensitively, so both are rank 0 (ties by index: line then Line). 'LinearDimension' is rank 2 (no case-sensitive prefix 'line'). 'Limit' does not match.
Every name lowercases to the query, so all are rank 0. Exact case is NOT a rank inside group 0; ties fall to original index.
'Pointer' and 'Point' start with 'Po' (rank 1); 'point' does not (rank 2). Rank-1 sorted by lowercase: 'point' < 'pointer'.
Duplicate names are distinct table entries and are all returned. 'limit' < 'line' lowercase, so Limit leads; the two Line entries keep index order.
Empty prefix returns no matches (reference behaviour).
Case-insensitive prefix matches; 'line' does not start with 'LIN' case-sensitively, so rank 2, still returned.

fuzzy.derivation: 'abacus' is an exact prefix and is excluded from inexact. zAB, zABCDE, cab all have first=1 span=2; usage desc puts zABCDE(5) first; cab and zAB tie on usage and length, so lowercase 'cab' < 'zab'.
Both fuzzy-match with first=1 span=2. Usage descending: yab (i64 MAX) before zab (i64 MIN). Neither starts with 'ab'.
Keys (first,span): axxxxb (0,6), xaxb (1,3), xxab (2,2). First position sorts before span, so the widest but earliest match leads.
Both first=1. Span 2 (xab) beats span 3 (xaxb) even though xaxb has usage 100.
Both first=1 span=2. Usage 5 beats the shorter length of xab.
Both first=1 span=2, no usage. Length 4 (xabz) beats length 5 (xabaa) even though 'xabaa' is lexicographically smaller.
Identical keys on every stage; duplicates are both returned in index order.
Greedy leftmost subsequence: xaxxa -> a@1, a@4 (first 1, span 4); xxaa -> a@2, a@3 (first 2, span 2). First position decides, so xaxxa leads.
'q' does not occur in 'xab'.
A four-letter subsequence cannot fit in a three-letter name.
Empty typed text yields two empty lists.
'abc' starts with 'ab', so it lives only in the exact group; 'xab' is the single inexact match.
Keys (first,span): xaxxxb (1,5), xxab (2,2). Start decides before usage 1000 on xxab can apply.
Equal first=1; span 2 before span 3 with no usage at all.
Equal first and span. yab has usage 1 and comes first even though it has the higher index.
xab is missing from usage so counts as 0; yab is -5. Descending usage puts xab first.
Equal first and span; length 4 before length 5 although 'xabaa' sorts first alphabetically.
Equal first, span, usage and length 4; lowercase 'xaba' < 'xabb'.
Lowercase names are identical and every key ties, so original index decides.
'ABc' starts with 'ab' case-insensitively, so it is exact; 'xabc' is inexact.
Usage cannot move a name from the exact group into the inexact group or reorder across groups.

Greedy leftmost: aaxb matches a@0 then b@3 (first 0, span 4); axb matches a@0 then b@2 (first 0, span 3). Span 3 leads even though the first letter is the same. (A first draft used 'axab', whose b is at index 3, giving span 4 and a tie; the reference was right and the fixture was wrong.)
'ax' starts with 'a' (exact). 'xa' is inexact at (1,1). 'b' contains no 'a'.
